hypothesis: Generating and recognizing active-step timeout messages through one core contract will keep infrastructure stalls out of improver actionability and health-review coverage gaps even when timeout accounting wording changes.

metricsCompared.name: latest actionable run after active-runtime timeout
metricsCompared.baseline: The current run packet advanced latestActionableRunAt to 2026-07-27T07:45:57.818Z from a progress-reviewer timeout that the gate contract classifies as infrastructure.
metricsCompared.candidate: A live aggregation replay excludes that timeout and reports the genuine eval-harness terminal failure at 2026-07-27T02:53:30.517Z.

metricsCompared.name: agent-step timeouts retained for diagnosis
metricsCompared.baseline: The current run packet listed two historical progress-reviewer timeouts and omitted the new active-runtime timeout.
metricsCompared.candidate: The live aggregation replay lists all three progress-reviewer timeouts, including run 2026-07-27T03-25-55-661Z-progress-reviewer-lk8i7q.

metricsCompared.name: focused timeout contract coverage
metricsCompared.baseline: Autonomy regression fixtures exercised only the pre-active-runtime timeout message, so the production wording drift was invisible.
metricsCompared.candidate: Four focused files pass 64 tests covering canonical message generation, durable-record recognition, strict nonmatching, improver aggregation, and health-review suppression.

rationale: The candidate restores the documented infrastructure exclusion against the exact retained failure and centralizes the producer/consumer contract without broad timeout matching. It preserves historical timeout visibility, leaves the genuine eval-harness failure actionable, and does not claim to resolve the underlying progress-reviewer dead letter.
